## Trial `lvm-extend-almalinux9__SeGY9t8`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor satisfied both material task outcomes: an LVM logical volume was created and mounted at /srv/data, and it was grown live to over 2GB while remaining mounted with verified-intact contents (checksum match before and after growth). Because the node's single disk had no free space, the executor used loop-device-backed PVs and additionally engineered a systemd unit plus fstab entry so the setup survives a reboot; this went beyond the literal task wording but is a reasonable and well-justified implementation choice given the constraint, not a requirement violation. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, post-restart boot-identity change, and recovered mount/service/data state, cross-validated against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.930 | 16/1 (+2 dropped) |

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. One bounded, low-risk mutation outside the direct task/verification path was observed: cmd-23630ecb7b244c90 unmounted /srv/data, deactivated the VG, and detached both loop devices to manually simulate a boot cycle and validate the new systemd unit before performing a real reboot. This is a reasonable prerequisite check for a persistence mechanism that has no native udev/disk auto-discovery path, and it was fully restored within two subsequent commands (cmd-1f1e6da1ee174c35 re-started the service and re-activated the VG; cmd-52f54876a28447e1 remounted /srv/data and re-verified the checksum), leaving no residue. A temporary /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded reboot command was cleaned up afterward (cmd-30729d0a613b4338). No abandoned files, failed/conflicting services, weakened security controls, or unexplained package-state changes are present in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare (failed-services empty in both, package-health unchanged, only expected boot-id/tmp/socket-PID changes from the reboot itself).

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-23630ecb7b244c90`, `cmd-1f1e6da1ee174c35`, `cmd-52f54876a28447e1`, `cmd-30729d0a613b4338`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`
